info.title: Tenant device-enabled entry HTTP contract
info.description: B2 device entry profile. Includes device-auth login/refresh/challenge/conditional selection and all tenant self-service device routes. It replaces ordinary login/refresh routes for the same entry. No scan endpoints. Admission is host-trusted and restricted to provision and registration-result. Registration recovery uses the original request id and fresh admission authorization; complete is a one-time write and must be resolved by reading registration-result. The B2 grant binds tenant/client/device, not entry identity; entry_id isolation is local to SDK state.

post.description: Device-enabled v2 entry: this route replaces ordinary login/refresh for that entry. Device proof is optional or required by the configured entry policy; when present it binds the original raw JSON bytes, method, external path and audience using EMBEDDED-IDP-DEVICE-AUTH-V2. Include x-embedded-idp-tenant-id with all five proof headers: x-device-id, x-device-key-id, x-device-challenge, x-device-signature, and x-device-signed-at. Without proof, do not send the tenant assertion header.

get.description: Lists only devices bound to the authenticated subject, tenant and client. limit/cursor are query parameters; cursor is scoped.

post.description: Completes device registration using the public JWK and challenge/signature fields in this JSON body. The registration signature is verified by the device service; HTTP device-proof headers and admission grant are not used by this route. Completion is not idempotent: the one-time challenge and registration are consumed atomically. After an unknown response, query registration-result; do not replay the old signature. A challenge response alone does not prove that its challenge was stored or that completion is possible.

Bearer subject authentication and all five device proof headers are required: x-device-id, x-device-key-id, x-device-challenge, x-device-signature, and x-device-signed-at. The host-bound EMBEDDED-IDP-DEVICE-REQUEST-V2 profile verifies signature over original raw JSON bytes, HTTP method, externally visible path (including host prefix), audience and tenant; query strings are rejected and JSON reserialization is not used. An optional x-embedded-idp-tenant-id must match the authenticated tenant.

get.description: Returns only an operation visible to authenticated subject, tenant and client.

post.description: Issues a tenant/device/purpose challenge; HTTP 200 only returns a generated challenge and does not prove it was stored or that registration can complete. Registration challenge purpose is device_registration; only a successful complete followed by registration-result confirms completion.

Requires a host-validated short-lived admission grant bound by the host to tenant, client and device; each call is reauthorized. Provision is idempotent only when retried with the original registration_request_id and identical tenant/device/name/public JWK under the same registration scope. Reusing the id with changed fields conflicts. No query credential; the grant is carried in x-embedded-idp-device-admission.

post.description: Requires a fresh host-validated short-lived admission grant on every call, bound to the same tenant, client and device. The grant's stable registration scope and registration_request_id select the record; a changed scope cannot read it. No query credential; the grant is carried in x-embedded-idp-device-admission. Entry identity is not part of this server-side grant scope.

post.description: Requires the current authenticated subject and an active device binding, plus Ed25519 signatures from both the current and proposed keys over the same DEVICE-KEY-ROTATION-V2 bytes. expected_key_id and expected_key_version are compare-and-swap preconditions; the service verifies the one-time device_key_rotation challenge, retires the old key, activates the new key, and appends audit atomically. This operation has no idempotency key or receipt; retrying the old challenge/signatures fails. After an unknown response, read the current device pointer and both relevant key metadata under the same active binding. A challenge response does not prove its nonce was persisted.
Authenticated subject; expected binding version and operation id provide concurrency/idempotency controls.
